decisive_items: submucosal mass on the lesser curvature of the stomach
low-echo lesion with regular, clear margins confined to the submucosal layer
vascular signal extending from the periphery into the center of the lesion
response.rationale: Large solitary submucosal gastric mass with clear margins, central vascularity, and chronic GI bleeding is most consistent with GIST. Leiomyoma can appear similar on EUS but is less vascular and less likely at this size; carcinoid is typically smaller or multiple and often associated with neuroendocrine/hypergastrinemia features.

rejected.why: Gastric carcinoid is less likely given the large solitary size, prominent central vascular pattern, and absence of typical neuroendocrine or multiple-lesion features.
